stories.headline: Home Ministry widens passport and visa exemptions for some foreigners living in India
stories.summary: The Home Ministry has notified an amendment to the Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) Order. It exempts persecuted Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis and Christians from Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan who arrived by 31 December 2024 from passport rules, though they still need a visa to stay. Registered Sri Lankan Tamils, Tibetans and some long-staying Pakistani nationals are also covered, and Indians travelling to Nepal or Bhutan can use listed ID instead of a passport.

stories.headline: Iran's security chief meets Putin, says no talks with US until seven demands are met
stories.summary: Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, met Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Thursday and handed over a letter from Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. Rezaei says Tehran will not negotiate with Washington or reopen the Strait of Hormuz until the US meets Iran's seven conditions, which include lifting sanctions and releasing frozen assets. He says Putin repeated Russia's readiness to help end the war.
stories.why_it_matters: Iran's hard line keeps Hormuz shut and the risk of renewed US strikes alive, which keeps oil near $100 and pressures India's import bill.
stories.note: Meeting confirmed by Al Jazeera and All India Radio; the conditions are Iran's own position.

image.alt: Vladimir Putin greets Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei in Moscow

impact.why: Iran refuses to reopen Hormuz before its demands are met, keeping supply risk high.

stories.headline: Arab parties back Eisenkot, giving him 67 Knesset nominations to be Israel's PM
stories.summary: The Joint List and Ra'am told President Isaac Herzog they recommend Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government, lifting his support to 67 of 120 lawmakers. Netanyahu's bloc holds 53 seats. Eisenkot had earlier ruled out Arab parties as coalition partners, and the nominee will have 28 days, plus a possible 14, to form a government.
stories.why_it_matters: It puts Benjamin Netanyahu on course to lose power, which could reshape Israel's war policy and Middle East diplomacy.

stories.headline: Rupee climbs to six-month high near 94 per dollar on foreign inflows
stories.summary: The rupee opened weaker at 94.50 but turned around to trade near 94.00 per dollar by early afternoon, its strongest level in about six months, after closing at 94.47 on Thursday. Dealers credit heavy foreign buying of Indian shares, after foreign investors bought about ₹14,975 crore of stocks on Thursday. The dollar index was up about 0.3% near 101.9 ahead of tonight's US jobs report.
stories.why_it_matters: A firmer rupee eases the cost of oil and other imports and signals foreign money is returning to India.
stories.note: Intraday high reported as 94.06 by Business Standard and about 94.08 by FXStreet; level near 94.00 from Yahoo Finance at 1:46 PM IST.

impact.why: Strong foreign equity inflows are adding dollar supply.
A stronger rupee trims the value of IT exporters' dollar earnings.

stories.headline: Sensex tops 80,000 as Indian stocks shrug off Asia's chip crash
stories.summary: The Sensex was up about 850 points, or 1.1%, near 80,160 and the Nifty up about 1.1% near 24,800 at 1:45 PM, even as Korea and Japan fell about 6%. Foreign investors bought about ₹14,975 crore of Indian shares on Thursday, while domestic funds sold about ₹10,444 crore. Private banks, consumer durables and pharma led; midcaps, smallcaps, capital goods and realty lagged.
stories.why_it_matters: India is acting as a haven as money rotates out of global AI and chip stocks, a shift that supports both the Nifty and the rupee.

image.alt: The Bombay Stock Exchange tower in Mumbai seen through trees

impact.why: Record-sized foreign buying is flowing into large caps, led by private banks.
Foreign equity inflows add dollar supply.

stories.headline: Asia closes deep in red: Kospi down 6% to 5,060, Nikkei down 6% to 57,435
stories.summary: Update: Korea's Kospi ended about 6% lower at 5,059.69 after a trading halt and a brief dip below 5,000, and Japan's Nikkei closed down 5.96% at 57,434.77, deep in a bear market. Chip makers such as SK Hynix, Samsung and Kioxia led the losses after Wall Street's AI sell-off. Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell a milder 1.2%.
stories.note: Closing levels from KED Global and Yahoo Finance; earlier intraday report from CNBC.

impact.why: The chip sell-off keeps spreading across markets.

stories.headline: Gold falls about ₹2,000 on MCX on Dhanteras as dollar firms
stories.summary: MCX December gold fell roughly ₹2,000 to around ₹1.42 lakh per 10 grams on Friday, Dhanteras, with silver down about ₹3,000 per kg. Comex gold slipped about 1.3% to near $4,060 an ounce on profit-taking and a firmer dollar ahead of US jobs data.
stories.why_it_matters: Lower prices on Dhanteras, a top day for gold buying in India, could lift festive jewellery demand.
stories.note: Intraday levels vary by report time.

impact.why: Profit-taking and a firmer dollar weigh on prices.

stories.headline: Brent hovers near $100 as analysts weigh renewed US-Iran fighting
stories.summary: Brent rose about 1.7% to near $99.90 and US crude to about $91.70 in Asian trade, CNBC said. Rapidan Energy's Bob McNally put the odds of renewed fighting at 80% now that the US midterms are over, while Iran reported three more tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday. Brent was near $98.90 by early afternoon in India.
stories.why_it_matters: Oil near $100 raises India's import bill and keeps pressure on inflation.
stories.note: Single source: CNBC. Tanker attacks are Iran's report; not independently confirmed.

impact.why: Risk of renewed US-Iran fighting adds a supply premium.

stories.headline: FDA approves J&J's Rybrevant Faspro for advanced head and neck cancer
stories.summary: The US FDA granted accelerated approval to Johnson & Johnson's under-the-skin amivantamab, Rybrevant Faspro, for head and neck squamous cell cancer that has come back or spread after chemotherapy and immunotherapy. In a 102-patient trial, 42% of patients responded, and over half of those responses lasted six months or more. It is not approved for HPV-linked throat cancer.
stories.why_it_matters: Patients with this cancer have few options once standard treatments fail.

impact.why: A new approved use widens the cancer drug's market.

stories.headline: GRSE delivers home-built anti-submarine warship Amini to the Navy
stories.summary: Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers of Kolkata has handed the Navy Amini, an anti-submarine shallow water craft it designed and built. The waterjet-driven ship carries lightweight torpedoes, Indian-made rocket launchers and sonars, and can also lay mines and watch the coast. More than 80% of it is made in India.

impact.why: Another on-schedule warship delivery supports its order execution.

forex_results.why: The BoE raised its rate by 0.25 point to 4%, as expected.

forex_results.title: MPC Official Bank Rate Votes
forex_results.why: All nine members voted to hike (one wanted 0.5 point), more hawkish than the 7-0-2 forecast; supports the pound.

forex_results.title: Monetary Policy Summary
forex_results.why: The MPC hiked to stop energy costs spreading to other prices and said policy is not on a pre-set path.

forex_results.title: BOE Monetary Policy Report
forex_results.why: The BoE now sees UK inflation near 5% by mid-2027 and activity stronger than expected.

forex_results.title: BOE Gov Bailey Speaks
forex_results.why: Bailey said he would not sign up to a 'two and done' path and saw an argument for a further rise.

forex_results.title: Unemployment Claims
forex_results.why: Claims fell to 189,000, below the 197,000 forecast, a sign of a tight job market that supports the dollar.

forex_results.title: BOC Gov Macklem Speaks
forex_results.why: Macklem said rates may need to rise further after the hike to 2.5%, while moving carefully; supportive for the Canadian dollar.

forex_results.title: Annual Budget Release
forex_results.why: The deficit came in a little below the spring estimate of C$65.3B, a mild positive for the Canadian dollar.
